title: Intelligently fallback to available agent when default agent has exhausted usage
head: 6e1334a5160b
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Most supported defaults have no usage record to evaluate
leads.consequence: At this head, the only stock agent usage collectors are claude and codex (fireworks is a third collector but not a launcher). The other 12 supported defaults receive score 50 merely for having a command, so an exhausted or signed-out default among them is retained, and its quota is never checked. Pi/OMP and OpenCode sessions are even attributed to the Claude/Codex subscription collectors, not to per-harness quota files. With no default, an unmeasured agent also qualifies before prompting for one. The next invocation reads the same absent record and makes the same choice.

leads.summary: Executability is mistaken for a ready agent, including the always-packaged OpenClaw helper
leads.consequence: On a normal provision, ~/.local/bin contains executable mise stubs for agents not yet downloaded or authenticated; shutil.which sees those and a missing JSON earns score 50. The first candidate by list order can therefore initiate an installation/login rather than continue a crash diagnosis. Even after stubs are removed, omarchy-launch-openclaw is packaged irrespective of whether optional openclaw is installed, so with an exhausted Codex and no other available CLI the resolver prints fallback to openclaw, but the subsequent omarchy-cmd-missing openclaw exits with status 1. No agent window opens and clicking the crash notification again repeats the failure. Check actual launchability/readiness and the same PATH the launcher uses, not just executable presence.

leads.summary: A real Claude record can be ready while the sign-in is missing
leads.consequence: Claude's collector sets ready from historical local prompts or a limit, while a missing access token produces usageStatusText='Waiting for auth'. Once any history exists, ready=true and the new test does not recognize that status, so a signed-out Claude remains the chosen default even with an available Codex record. The selector never tries the available Codex; Claude still needs authentication to use that subscription, and the next --fallback invocation repeats the selection. Treat the producer's Waiting for auth state as unready rather than equating ready with authentication.
leads.triage: corroborated by Opus score table ('Waiting for auth' scores 95, kept); folded into F3 table and impact

leads.summary: Expired usage windows and failed refreshes leave old limits authoritative indefinitely
leads.consequence: Records include updatedAt and a limit's resetsAt, but the resolver checks neither. The updater only replaces a JSON file on successful collection and leaves the previous one intact on failure; a 100%-used limit from before its reset will keep selecting a different agent although the default may have recovered. An old record with available headroom can conversely retain an exhausted default. This persists until a successful refresh and affects every --fallback/crash launch while the collector cannot refresh. Compare record freshness/reset timestamps or decline to treat stale percentages as authoritative.

leads.summary: A usage-probe failure is treated as an unavailable coding agent
leads.consequence: Codex emits 'Codex limits unavailable' on an app-server RPC exception after starting its CLI, and Claude emits 'Claude limits unavailable' when an OAuth quota probe fails without cached windows, including transport failures for which it sets retryAdvised. Neither state proves that the coding agent itself cannot run. The new substring test treats both as zero score, bypasses that default and can launch an unconfigured/cold alternative. Retrying while the usage API is down repeats this choice; distinguish an unknown quota from an unusable CLI or exhausted allowance.

leads.summary: Open remote-agent PR #12059 conflicts in both launch and crash entry points
leads.consequence: #12059 adds --local and a remote host to omarchy-agent and changes the crash handoff to --local --prompt so local cores stay on this machine. This PR adds --fallback and changes that same call to --fallback --prompt. The diverged heads produce 3 conflict sections in agent and 1 in crash with git merge-file against their shared base; neither side alone retains both behaviors. A resolution must pass both flags for crash and decide whether local quota should pick an agent that is installed/running on the remote host. The other PR is MERGEABLE with its own base, which does not resolve this pairwise conflict. Unresolved merged code could not be executed.

leads.summary: One valid-JSON malformed balance can abort the resolver and silently launch the exhausted default
leads.consequence: The updater validates JSON syntax, not record schema, and this repository explicitly permits other record writers. A balance object with remaining='invalid' is caught by the first float conversion but retried unguarded at line 127, raising ValueError. The command substitution exits nonzero, prints a Python traceback on stderr, leaves resolved_agent empty, then Bash (without set -e) carries on launching the original agent with status 0. A noniterable nonempty limits value similarly raises during the loop. In a crash action this means a terminal running the exhausted agent after a traceback, and repeated clicks behave the same until the bad JSON changes. Validate types once and handle resolver failure explicitly.

leads.summary: Alternate executable names qualify an agent that the launcher cannot execute
leads.consequence: The resolver accepts a cursor executable as proof of cursor-agent, and gemini as proof of agy. The downstream launch checks command -v for the canonical cursor-agent or agy and builds that exact command, not the executable found by Python. With only cursor present and its usage record healthy, it prints a fallback to cursor-agent, then returns status 1 'cursor-agent is not installed'; no agent starts, and retries do not help. The same condition holds for agy/gemini. Only score the executable that the command case will actually invoke.

leads.summary: Several overlapping Antigravity collector PRs would publish a stem this resolver ignores
leads.consequence: #11989, #8873 and #10400 each add a collector named omarchy-agent-usage-antigravity with id antigravity. The updater writes antigravity.json, whereas AGENTS checks only agy.json and gemini.json; an exhausted or unauthenticated agy default retains guessed score 50 rather than reading their real result. The sibling #8479 uses id agy and does match, so this is conditional on which collector PR lands. Include the antigravity stem when integrating any of the three alternatives.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator (#10400 collector AGENT_ID='antigravity', coord/hunter-verify-prs.txt); Opus had #11989 and #8873; #10400 added to F6 note

leads.consequence: Without a configured default, the new resolver sets default_score=0 then selects the highest scoring installed command before reaching the -z $agent / --pick setup branch. A direct 'omarchy agent --fallback --pick' therefore can launch an unchosen agent (unattended and with auto-approval) instead of opening the picker; an explicit --fallback --inline with no default launched the first test stub claude with status 0. The crash watcher independently suppresses notifications until a default is configured, so this does not make no-default crash notifications work. Preserve the no-default gate before scoring, or specify a separate opt-in policy for choosing one.

leads.summary: Previously literal prompts beginning with --fallback now disappear or trigger selection
leads.consequence: Before this change, 'omarchy-agent-prompt --fallback' supplied the literal prompt '--fallback' through --prompt. Now the leading flag loop consumes it and, with no remaining words, emits Usage and exits 1; '--fallback something' silently starts fallback mode rather than forwarding those words as one prompt. A caller can work around this with a separate delimiter/prompt option, but the script does not provide one. The same option-like prompt after an ordinary first word remains literal. A synthetic baseline returned status 0 and forwarded '--prompt --fallback'; the head returned status 1 with Usage. Accept '--' or a documented literal-prompt escape.
leads.triage: already in Opus report (judged negligible); kept as one Verified parsing sentence, not a finding

leads.summary: New supported defaults added by overlapping PRs remain outside the hardcoded resolver
leads.consequence: #11367 adds selectable mcode, an mcode usage collector and a launch case; the pairwise merge of its agent script with this PR's agent script has no conflict and contains both the new mcode case and the unchanged 14-member AGENTS list. If mcode is the selected default, the 'unknown default' branch gives its executable score 50 regardless of an exhausted mcode.json record, so --fallback retains the exhausted mcode. #11444 adds GitLab Duo in the same new-default class (though that PR currently reports conflicts against its own target). Roster additions need a matching usage mapping or a non-hardcoded registration mechanism.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator (#11367 adds mcode to omarchy-agent and default-agent; unknown-default branch bin/omarchy-agent:139-141 scores 50); added to F6 note

leads.summary: The new tests pass when ranking is discarded and when crash context is dropped
leads.consequence: Case 4 always leaves Cursor as the sole high-scoring alternative, so sorting candidates to prefer cursor-agent regardless of percent still passes all seven assertions. The crash case checks only that the terminal starts cursor-agent, not that --prompt and the diagnose-crash skill reach it; deleting --prompt '$prompt' from the crash handoff also passes all seven. Both plausible mistakes defeat advertised features without a failing test. Add a competing measured candidate and inspect the crash launch argv, including prompt contents and skill path, using byte-preserving argv logs.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus, confirmed by its own mutant runs (opus/followup-1.md); published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: The AI manual still promises the default agent for every crash diagnosis
leads.consequence: The manual's crash workflow says a clicked notification is handed to 'your default agent'; after this PR the handoff explicitly passes --fallback and may pick someone else. It also documents prompt launches without mentioning the new opt-in --fallback examples available through command help. Readers troubleshooting a different agent in a crash notification have no explanation in the manual. Update the crash paragraph and add a short opt-in fallback example and limitations.

'Never have a record' is too strong: the usage directory accepts records from any writer (shell/plugins/agents/README.md:44-45). 'Always score 50' holds only when the agent is installed (bin/omarchy-agent:76-78 returns -1 otherwise).
flags.fix: Of the listed agents, only `claude` and `codex` have in-tree collectors, so on a stock install the others have no record and score 50 when installed.

flags.claim: "Sign-in expired": Saved access token lapsed. Claude Code refreshes it when it starts (`omarchy-agent-usage-claude:804-821`)
flags.why: The collector sets this status from the access token's expiresAt alone (:813-815). It cannot tell a routine lapse from an expired login, and its help text offers both 'Start Claude Code' and `claude auth login` (:816-820). The refresh is the routine case, not guaranteed. My own report had the same absolute wording (errata added).
flags.fix: Saved access token lapsed; Claude Code normally refreshes it when it starts.

flags.claim: "Claude limits unavailable": Limits probe failed, for example on HTTP 429 (`:841-846`); impact: 'or whose limits probe failed once, gets replaced'
flags.why: Lost qualifier. The status is written only when the probe fails and there are no cached limits from an earlier successful probe whose window is still open. The cache is read with infinite age and filtered by reset time (:800-802); if one exists, the limits are kept and the status stays empty (:841-843). One failed probe after a successful one does not cause a fallback.
flags.fix: Row: 'Limits probe failed with no cached limits still in their window, for example on HTTP 429'. Impact: '... or whose limits probe failed with no cached result ...'.
flags.disposition: real error; fixed: 'with no cached limits still in their window' and impact wording

flags.claim: Codex writes "Codex limits unavailable" on any RPC error or timeout (`omarchy-agent-usage-codex:544-561`)
flags.why: Only a timeout or another raised exception sets it (:559-561). rpc_request returns any reply with a matching id, including a JSON-RPC error reply, without raising (:477-495). That leaves no limits and an empty status, which scores 80.
flags.fix: Codex writes "Codex limits unavailable" when its RPC times out or otherwise fails with an exception (for example, the app-server exits).
flags.disposition: real error; fixed: 'times out or raises'

flags.claim: A fully signed-out Claude is kept.
flags.why: A signed-out record is kept only when `ready` is true, meaning local transcripts or cached limits exist (collector :890). A signed-out Claude with neither has ready=false and scores 0, which falls back.
flags.fix: A signed-out Claude with local usage history or cached limits is kept.
flags.disposition: real error; fixed: 'with usage history or cached limits'

flags.claim: With no default, `default_score` stays 0 and the first installed candidate is printed (`bin/omarchy-agent:133-141`).
flags.why: The highest-scoring installed candidate is printed, with ties in list order (:147-155). On a stock install with no records, that is the first stub (claude, as in S6). The cited range covers only the default scoring. My report had the same imprecision (errata added).
flags.fix: ... and the highest-scoring installed candidate is printed (`:133-155`); on a stock install without records that is the first stub in list order.

flags.claim: A default that is not in `AGENTS` scores 50 if its command is on PATH, whatever its usage record says (`:129-131`).
flags.why: Wrong citation; the statement itself is correct. The for-else branch that gives an unlisted default 50 is bin/omarchy-agent:139-141. Lines 129-131 are the 'ready and no status -> 80, else 50' lines inside evaluate_agent.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** `--fallback` works as described for the PR's own test data. Callers that do not pass the flag behave as on the base. The only caller that passes it is `omarchy-agent-crash`, the action behind "Click to diagnose with AI".

On a stock Omarchy install, though, Claude and Codex are the only listed agents with usage collectors. The resolver treats almost every other agent as available, can choose an agent the launcher then refuses, and treats several routine collector states as "exhausted". The notes below suggest tightening what counts as "available" before the crash click relies on it.

### Almost every listed agent counts as available on a stock install

An agent counts as installed when any of its command names resolves through `shutil.which` (`bin/omarchy-agent:70-78`). An installed agent with no usage record scores 50, and any score above 0 is a usable candidate (`:90-91`, `:147-151`). Candidates are sorted by score, so ties fall back to the order of the hard-coded `AGENTS` list (`:53-68`, `:153-155`).

On a stock install:
- `install/user/mise.sh` writes a lazy mise stub into `~/.local/bin` for 12 of the 14 listed agents (`omarchy-mise-install:51-57`). The stub installs the agent on first run.
- Of the listed agents, only `claude` and `codex` have in-tree usage collectors (`omarchy-agent-usage-update:55-62`), so the other installed agents normally have no record and score 50.

Sandboxed run with the stock stubs installed and the Claude default at 100% of its session window:

| Crash click, default Claude exhausted | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Stock stubs, no Codex record | `claude --permission-mode auto` | `codex --approve-for-me` (preinstalled stub) |
| Stock stubs, Codex record "Codex limits unavailable" | `claude --permission-mode auto` | `cursor-agent --yolo --trust agent` (stub) |
| Positive control: Codex record at 30% | `claude --permission-mode auto` | `codex --approve-for-me` |

**Impact:** a crash-notification click can install an agent the user never chose and start it in its auto-approve mode with the crash prompt. A newly installed agent may still need a sign-in. Agents without records (pi, opencode, omp) may also draw on the same Claude or Codex subscription that is already exhausted.

**Suggested change:** only count agents that are actually set up, for example by reusing the presence check `omarchy-default-agent` already has instead of `which`. Require a usage record that shows headroom before choosing a fallback candidate (today that limits fallback to Claude and Codex).

### The resolver can choose an agent the launcher refuses

The resolver accepts alternative command names: `omarchy-launch-openclaw` for OpenClaw, `cursor` for Cursor CLI and `gemini` for Antigravity (`bin/omarchy-agent:56, 58, 61`). The launcher then checks the agent name itself with `omarchy-cmd-missing` and exits 1 if it is missing (`:177-180`). `omarchy-launch-openclaw` ships with Omarchy in `/usr/share/omarchy/bin`, which the resolver searches explicitly, so OpenClaw always counts as installed.

```text
Sandboxed run: preinstalled stubs removed, only Claude installed, Claude at 100%

omarchy-agent-crash (this PR)
  -> resolver: "Default agent 'claude' has no available usage; falling back to 'openclaw'"
  -> launcher: "openclaw is not installed. Choose an installed agent with: omarchy default agent <name>"
  -> exit 1, nothing launched          (base: launches Claude)
```

A second run with Claude plus a `cursor` command, but no `cursor-agent`, did the same with `cursor-agent`.

**Impact:** notification actions run detached (`shell/plugins/notifications/Service.qml:364-368`), so from the crash notification the click would appear to do nothing (inferred from source, not observed on a live desktop), where the base opened the default agent.

**Suggested change:** check the same command name in the resolver that the launcher checks.

### Routine collector states are read as "exhausted"

The resolver scores an agent 0 when `usageStatusText` contains "expired", "sign in" or "unavailable", or when the highest `limits[].percent` is at least 1.0 (`bin/omarchy-agent:97, 100-114`). It does not read `updatedAt` or `resetsAt`. Scores from the PR's own `evaluate_agent` for Claude records:

| Claude record | Meaning in the collector | Score |
|---|---|---|
| "Sign-in expired", last-known 10% | Saved access token lapsed. Claude Code normally refreshes it when it starts (`omarchy-agent-usage-claude:804-821`) | 0 (fallback) |
| "Waiting for auth", last-known 10% | No credentials at all (`:809-812`) | 95 (kept) |
| "Claude limits unavailable" | Limits probe failed, for example on HTTP 429, with no cached limits still in their window (`:841-846`) | 0 (fallback) |
| Session 8%, weekly 31%, one model-scoped weekly window at 100% | Model-scoped windows share the `limits` array (`:669-708, 761`) | 0 (fallback) |
| 100% in a window that reset hours ago, record two days old | Disabled providers are never rewritten (`shell/plugins/agents/Main.qml:146-153`) | 0 (fallback) |

Codex writes "Codex limits unavailable" when its RPC probe times out or raises (`omarchy-agent-usage-codex:544-561`), with the same result. Sandboxed runs confirmed a fallback to Codex for the lapsed-token, probe-failure, model-scoped and stale cases, where the base launched Claude. The percent units themselves match the collectors (fractions, so 1.0 is 100%).

**Impact:** a Claude default that has not run for a while, or whose limits probe failed without cached limits, gets replaced by another agent. A fully signed-out Claude with usage history or cached limits is kept. Whether Claude Code keeps working on other models when only a model-scoped window is full was not verified here.

**Suggested change:** treat "limits unavailable", a lapsed access token and records whose window has reset or whose `updatedAt` is old as unknown, and keep the default for them. Only a current record that positively shows exhaustion should trigger a fallback. The trade-off is that a truly expired login would then also keep the default.

### `--fallback` picks an agent when no default is set

With no default, `default_score` stays 0 and the highest-scoring installed candidate is printed, the first in list order when scores tie (`bin/omarchy-agent:133-155`). The notice at `:161` is skipped because `$agent` is empty, and the existing no-default branch (`:171-175`: the picker with `--pick`, otherwise "Choose default agent with: omarchy default agent <name>") is never reached. That contradicts "Omarchy picks no agent for you" (`omarchy-default-agent:20-21`).

In a sandboxed run with stock stubs and no default, `omarchy agent crash <pid>`, `omarchy agent prompt --fallback "..."` and `omarchy-agent --pick --fallback` all launched Claude silently. The base printed the "Choose default agent" error, or opened the picker with `--pick`.

**Impact:** with no default set, these hand-run commands silently launch an agent the user did not choose. The crash notification itself is not affected, because it is only sent when a default exists (`omarchy-crash-watch:66-69`).

**Suggested change:** skip the resolver when no default is set, so the existing no-default flow still runs.

### Smaller notes

- **Malformed records:** `float(balance.get("remaining", 0) or 0)` at `bin/omarchy-agent:127` is outside the `try`, and `for lim in limits` (`:103`) assumes a list. A record for any installed agent with `"remaining": "n/a"` or `"limits": 5` raises out of the whole resolver, prints a traceback, and the exhausted default launches. In-tree collectors write valid records, but the agents README accepts records from any writer.
- **Third agent roster:** `AGENTS` repeats the roster in `omarchy-default-agent` and the `omarchy-agent` case statement. A default that is not in `AGENTS` scores 50 if its command is on PATH, whatever its usage record says (`:139-141`). Open PRs that add agents would also need an entry here. For example, #11367 adds `mcode` with its own usage collector, but an exhausted `mcode` default would still be kept. #11989, #8873 and #10400 add an Antigravity collector that writes `antigravity.json`, which this list does not read (it reads `agy` and `gemini`).
- **Docs:** `manual/17-ai.md:45` and the `omarchy-agent-crash` summary and comment (`:3, 9`) still say crashes go to the default agent. Nothing documents that another agent may be used, and hand-run `omarchy agent crash` has no way to turn the fallback off. The stderr notice "has no available usage" is also printed when the default is simply not installed.

**Optional test improvement:** two diagnostic mutants pass all 7 cases of `test/shell.d/agent-fallback-test.sh`. One resolver ignores scores and always prefers `cursor-agent`.
